item.title: Iran war’s oil shock fuels GOP political anxiety
item.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Tuesday would be “our most intense day of strikes,” after President Trump sent conflicting messages about the administration’s plans.

item.title: U.S. orders more diplomats to leave Middle East
item.summary: The State Department’s most recent directives apply to personnel in Turkey and Saudi Arabia, underscoring the ongoing threat posed by Iranian counterattacks.

item.title: Trump’s wearing of baseball cap during dignified transfer draws criticism
item.summary: President Trump faced continued blowback for wearing a USA-emblazoned cap during a dignified transfer ceremony for soldiers killed in the war with Iran.

item.title: Early Iran strikes cost $5.6 billion in munitions, Pentagon estimates
item.summary: The figure, accounting for the war’s first two days, is likely to intensify concerns in Congress that U.S. forces are churning through a scarce supply of advanced weaponry.

item.title: A wartime presidency defined by Trump’s unique political style
item.summary: President Trump is recasting the role of wartime leader in his image, breaking from generations of practice as he attacks his domestic enemies and revels in memes.

item.title: Australia grants asylum to 5 Iranian soccer players after Trump pressure
item.summary: The late-night visa approval came after a days-long operation, authorities said. The players had been criticized back home after they stood silently during the Iranian anthem.

item.title: After slashing federal jobs, Trump administration ramps up hiring
item.summary: The hiring push is unfolding under new rules designed to give the White House greater influence over the government’s 2 million-person civilian workforce.

item.title: Consumer advocates, Democrats denounce Live Nation deal as inadequate
item.summary: Officials have alleged that Ticketmaster and parent company Live Nation Entertainment held an illegal monopoly over concerts and other live events.

item.title: In Trump’s Washington, Congress has little power left
item.summary: Trump’s second presidency has accelerated the growth of executive power at the expense of the legislative branch, raising concerns about the balance of powers.

item.title: White House fires GOP NTSB member, who calls it ‘political hit job’
item.summary: J. Todd Inman frequently represented the National Transportation Safety Board in news conferences after the deadly American Airlines crash in D.C. last year.
